ca_spring_wall.blurb: Spring Wall is a single-pitch bolted wall in the Horseshoe Piles group above Horseshoe Lake, near Lake George outside Mammoth Lakes, at roughly 9,200 feet. Its 13 climbs run from easy fifth class up to one 5.12, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.11, so strong intermediates will find the most to do. Lines are long single pitches on clean, crisp granite, and the wall stays quiet because the walk in is steep and a bit fiddly. Good for a summer day in the high Sierra, when the lower valley is hot.
ca_spring_wall.parking_note: Leave the car in the Lake George parking area, where the Crystal Lake Trail begins.
ca_spring_wall.approach: Follow the Crystal Lake Trail uphill for about ten minutes until you see big water tanks, then leave the trail toward the tanks and cross the ridge beyond them. Expect 15 to 20 minutes overall, with steep ground and loose gravel in places.

ca_pixie_boulder.blurb: Pixie Boulder is a single, roughly 15-foot block at the foot of Pixie Rock in Indian Cove, in the lower, warmer north side of Joshua Tree National Park. It holds 13 problems, mostly in the easy range from VB to V3, with a couple of much harder lines at V6 and V7 for projecting. The block has a steeper side and a slabbier side, and the ground around it is flat, so pads and spotters are easy to arrange. The stone is a bit crumbly in places, so test your holds. Fall through early spring is the comfortable window.

ca_the_mortuary.blurb: The Mortuary is a small single-pitch crag set in a corner that looks north-west, below Deadman Buttress, at Chipmunk Flat along Highway 108 near Sonora Pass, around 9,200 feet. Its 13 routes are almost all trad, with one sport line, and they range from an easy 5.4 up to 5.11, with the largest group at 5.10. Beginners can find something here alongside the harder lines. Because the corner faces north-west it sits in shade for much of the day, which makes it a handy refuge when the weather is hot.

ca_sw_face_center_the_solarium.blurb: The Solarium is the middle part of the southwest face of Little Hunk in the Echo Rock area of central Joshua Tree, at about 4,200 feet. It mixes 6 sport routes, 4 trad and 3 top-rope lines on mostly slabby granite. Grades start at 5.1 and reach 5.11, but the bulk sits in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers who want moderate to mid-hard face work. The base is elevated with good views, the approach is short, and the face is calmer than the busy Monkey Business Wall beside it.
ca_sw_face_center_the_solarium.parking_note: Use the big gravel lot near Echo Tee.
ca_sw_face_center_the_solarium.approach: A quick walk from the gravel lot: take the trail east past the south end of Echo Rock.

ca_zebra_cliffs_east_face.blurb: The east face of the Zebra Cliffs is a brown band of rock on a small plateau near Jumbo Rocks in Joshua Tree National Park. Most of its 13 routes are single-pitch trad, with two sport lines. Grades begin at 5.8 and run mostly through the 5.9 and 5.10 range, with one 5.11, and several of the 5.10s are known to feel stiff. The face takes morning and early afternoon sun and then falls into shade, giving a pleasant spot to climb through the cooler months.
ca_zebra_cliffs_east_face.parking_note: Park in the last loop of the Jumbo Rocks campground (the G Loop).
ca_zebra_cliffs_east_face.approach: From the campground loop, walk roughly half a mile south. The cliffs appear on your right along the plateau.

ca_twin_towers.blurb: Twin Towers is a tall wall of bolted sport climbing within the old quarry zone of Auburn State Recreation Area, near Sacramento. All 13 routes are sport, and the grades lean hard: one 5.9, nine at 5.11 and three at 5.12. The style is sustained endurance climbing on good edges, so it suits people who are already comfortable leading in the low 5.11s. The base is reached by walking up the left side of the main quarry area and following a short trail beyond Wreckage Wall.

ca_right_side_5.blurb: The Right Side is the second crag at Squirrel Creek, in the Danland area of Sequoia and Kings Canyon, at about 3,300 feet. Its obvious landmark is a triangular roof split by two cracks. The 13 climbs blend slabs with cracks: 7 trad, 4 sport, one top-rope and one aid line. Grades stretch from 5.7 to 5.11, and a good number sit around 5.10 and 5.11, so it works best for confident leaders. It is set in a forested creek setting, a short walk beyond the first crag.
